title: How many outcomes are there really?

prereqs.why: The whole question is what the set of outcomes is before any probability is computed.

statement:
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled, **one red and one blue**, and the pair of numbers is recorded.

How many outcomes are in the sample space $\Omega$?

Be careful: the dice are distinguishable, so $(\text{red } 2, \text{blue } 5)$ and $(\text{red } 5, \text{blue } 2)$ are different outcomes.
hints: An outcome here is a *pair*: what the red die shows and what the blue die shows. Write one down and count how much freedom each part has.
The red die has six possibilities. For each of those, how many does the blue die have?
This is the multiplication principle: independent choices multiply. $6$ choices followed by $6$ choices.

payload.label: $|\Omega| =$
payload.syntax: A whole number. Arithmetic is fine: 6*6 is read as 36.
